jobs.title: Forensics - Crisis and Investigations - Cyber Response - Manager

reading.body:
Digital forensics hiring in this sample is a federal and consulting market, not a hyperscaler market: two of three postings are US government roles and the third is a Big Four advisory position.

The three roles span entry to manager, with posted salary ranges from $87,362 to $192,300. Two sit in the Washington, D.C. orbit, Fort Meade and McLean, and one in Richmond, California. All three are categorized as security work with a digital forensics function, which places them in the investigative and incident response side of the field rather than in model training or infrastructure.

Nothing here ties these jobs to compute buildout, data center construction, or power procurement. Forensics demand is driven by investigations, litigation, and federal casework, and this sample is too small to show a trend in either direction. What it does show is that the employers paying for this skill are government agencies and consultancies, not AI labs.

The data covers three postings collected on October 6, 2026, from USAJobs and Jooble. It does not include application volumes, offer rates, or whether these roles were filled, so it cannot speak to how competitive the market is.
